subject: c12-pe
scope: CBSE Class XII Physical Education (048) 2026-27 written/theory Board-exam preparation for a private candidate; practical/internal-assessment preparation excluded.

weightage.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease
Physical Education and Sports for CWSN

reference.label: Management of Sporting Events — Tip 1
reference.text: Memorise the five management functions: planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling.

reference.label: Management of Sporting Events — Tip 2
reference.text: Keep committee responsibilities separated into before-event, during-event and after-event duties.

reference.label: Management of Sporting Events — Tip 3
reference.text: Practise knock-out fixtures, especially bye and seeding procedures, instead of only reading them.

reference.label: Management of Sporting Events — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep staircase, cyclic and tabular league methods distinct and know when each is used.

reference.label: Management of Sporting Events — Tip 5
reference.text: Revise intramural vs extramural tournaments and the listed community sports programmes.

reference.label: Children and Women in Sports — Tip 1
reference.text: Study the prescribed WHO exercise guidelines by age group.

reference.label: Children and Women in Sports — Tip 2
reference.text: Make a deformity → corrective measure table for knock knees, flat foot, round shoulders, lordosis, kyphosis, scoliosis and bow legs.

reference.label: Children and Women in Sports — Tip 3
reference.text: Separate the physical, psychological and social benefits of women's participation.

reference.label: Children and Women in Sports — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep menarche, menstrual dysfunction and female athlete triad as separate concepts.

reference.label: Children and Women in Sports — Tip 5
reference.text: Memorise the three components of the female athlete triad: osteoporosis, amenorrhea and eating disorders.

reference.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease — Tip 1
reference.text: Study yoga by lifestyle disease rather than memorising all asanas as one list.

reference.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease — Tip 2
reference.text: For every prescribed asana/pranayama, learn procedure, benefits and contraindications together.

reference.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease — Tip 3
reference.text: Use separate tables for obesity, diabetes, asthma, hypertension, and back pain/arthritis.

reference.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease — Tip 4
reference.text: Practise writing the correct asana list for a given disease without mixing conditions.

reference.label: Yoga as Preventive Measure for Lifestyle Disease — Tip 5
reference.text: Pay particular attention to contraindications because simply naming the asana is incomplete.

reference.label: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN — Tip 1
reference.text: Keep Special Olympics, Paralympics and Deaflympics clearly differentiated.

reference.label: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN — Tip 2
reference.text: Understand classification and divisioning as separate concepts.

reference.label: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN — Tip 3
reference.text: Learn inclusion through its meaning, need and implementation.

reference.label: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN — Tip 4
reference.text: Revise the advantages of physical activity for children with special needs.

reference.label: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN — Tip 5
reference.text: Prepare practical examples of strategies that make physical activities accessible.

reference.label: Sports and Nutrition — Tip 1
reference.text: Build a table of macro- and micronutrients with food sources and functions.

reference.label: Sports and Nutrition — Tip 2
reference.text: Keep nutritive and non-nutritive components distinct.

reference.label: Sports and Nutrition — Tip 3
reference.text: Revise balanced diet, healthy weight, dieting pitfalls, food intolerance and food myths together.

reference.label: Sports and Nutrition — Tip 4
reference.text: Separate pre-, during- and post-competition dietary requirements.

reference.label: Sports and Nutrition — Tip 5
reference.text: Use examples of foods and nutrients to strengthen recall instead of memorising definitions alone.

reference.label: Test and Measurement in Sports — Tip 1
reference.text: First identify the correct fitness test and the prescribed age/class group.

reference.label: Test and Measurement in Sports — Tip 2
reference.text: Learn each test's purpose, procedure, scoring and interpretation together.

reference.label: Test and Measurement in Sports — Tip 3
reference.text: Practise Harvard Step Test fitness-index calculations separately from conceptual questions.

reference.label: Test and Measurement in Sports — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep the Rikli & Jones six-test battery distinct from the SAI Khelo India tests.

reference.label: Test and Measurement in Sports — Tip 5
reference.text: Revise BMR computation and the Johnson–Methney movements as separate test-and-measurement topics.

reference.label: Physiology and Injuries in Sport — Tip 1
reference.text: Separate physiological factors determining fitness components from general effects of exercise.

reference.label: Physiology and Injuries in Sport — Tip 2
reference.text: Study muscular and cardio-respiratory effects in separate comparison tables.

reference.label: Physiology and Injuries in Sport — Tip 3
reference.text: Keep physiological changes due to ageing distinct from acute exercise effects.

reference.label: Physiology and Injuries in Sport — Tip 4
reference.text: Classify sports injuries before memorising examples.

reference.label: Physiology and Injuries in Sport — Tip 5
reference.text: Separate soft-tissue injuries from bone/joint injuries and learn the listed fracture types.

reference.label: Biomechanics and Sports — Tip 1
reference.text: Learn each of Newton's three laws with one clear sports application.

reference.label: Biomechanics and Sports — Tip 2
reference.text: Make a table for first-, second- and third-class levers with sports examples.

reference.label: Biomechanics and Sports — Tip 3
reference.text: Keep static and dynamic equilibrium distinct.

reference.label: Biomechanics and Sports — Tip 4
reference.text: Connect centre of gravity and friction to actual sports situations.

reference.label: Biomechanics and Sports — Tip 5
reference.text: Practise projectile-motion applications conceptually rather than memorising isolated statements.

reference.label: Psychology and Sports — Tip 1
reference.text: Learn personality definition and keep Jung classification separate from the Big Five theory.

reference.label: Psychology and Sports — Tip 2
reference.text: Distinguish motivation types from motivation techniques.

reference.label: Psychology and Sports — Tip 3
reference.text: Study exercise adherence through reasons, benefits and strategies.

reference.label: Psychology and Sports — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep aggression's meaning, concept and types clearly separated.

reference.label: Psychology and Sports — Tip 5
reference.text: Revise self-esteem, mental imagery, self-talk and goal setting as distinct psychological attributes.

reference.label: Training in Sports — Tip 1
reference.text: Keep talent identification and talent development as separate stages/concepts.

reference.label: Training in Sports — Tip 2
reference.text: Memorise micro, meso and macro cycles and understand their relationship.

reference.label: Training in Sports — Tip 3
reference.text: Study strength, endurance and speed methods separately.

reference.label: Training in Sports — Tip 4
reference.text: Do the same for flexibility and coordinative ability methods.

reference.label: Training in Sports — Tip 5
reference.text: Understand the purpose and importance of circuit training rather than memorising only its definition.

mistakes: Mixing the five management functions, committee responsibilities or tournament procedures.
Confusing postural deformities with their corrective measures or mixing menarche, menstrual dysfunction and the female athlete triad.
Writing an asana/pranayama name without its prescribed procedure, benefits and contraindications.
Confusing Special Olympics, Paralympics and Deaflympics, or mixing classification, divisioning and inclusion.
Mixing macro/micronutrients, nutritive/non-nutritive components or pre/during/post-competition requirements.
Confusing age-group fitness batteries, test purpose, procedure, scoring/calculation and interpretation.
Mixing exercise effects with ageing changes or confusing soft-tissue and bone/joint injuries.
Confusing Newton's laws, levers, equilibrium, centre of gravity, friction and projectile motion in sports applications.
Confusing personality, motivation, exercise adherence, aggression and the listed psychological attributes.
Mixing talent identification/development, training cycles and methods for different fitness components.
order: Start with Management of Sporting Events and master tournament terminology and fixture procedures.
Study Children and Women in Sports and make a compact deformity-to-correction and concept comparison sheet.
Study Yoga by lifestyle condition, keeping procedure, benefits and contraindications together for every prescribed asana/pranayama.
Study CWSN with clear distinctions between organisations, classification/divisioning, inclusion, advantages and accessibility strategies.
Complete Sports and Nutrition with nutrient/component comparisons and pre-, during- and post-competition requirements.
Practise Test and Measurement through test identification, procedure, scoring and calculation questions.
Study Physiology and Injuries by separating system effects, ageing changes and injury classifications.
Study Biomechanics through law/lever/equilibrium/friction/projectile concept-to-sports applications.
Finish Psychology by connecting each definition or theory with its prescribed type, technique or attribute.
Finish Training by separating talent development, training cycles, component-specific methods and circuit training.
Revise all ten units using short-answer recall followed by concept/application and case-based practice.
Keep practical-file and practical-performance preparation separate from the 70-mark written-theory revision.
